chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr al-Anṣārī was in al-Madīnah, while the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله was in Makkah. When death approached him, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and the Muslims were praying toward Bayt al-Maqdis, al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr instructed that his face be turned toward the direction of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, toward the qiblah. He also bequeathed one-third of his wealth, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) came to be established by that.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ: the established prophetic tradition or normative practice
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: the sacred direction of orientation in worship
key_terms.بَيْتِ الْمَقْدِسِ: Bayt al-Maqdis, the direction toward which the Muslims were praying at that time
key_terms.بِثُلُثِ مَالِهِ: one-third of his wealth as a bequest

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for turning the dying person toward the qiblah and limiting a bequest to one-third of the estate?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that al-Barāʾ ibn Maʿrūr, at the time of his death, instructed that his face be turned toward the qiblah and that one-third of his wealth be given as a bequest. The report presents these actions as becoming part of the established sunnah (prophetic tradition), linking funeral orientation and the one-third bequest to early Islamic practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5428 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Muawiyah ibn Ammar from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

"Al-Bara' ibn Marur Al-Ansari was in Medina while the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca.
When death approached him (Al-Bara'), and while the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) and the Muslims were still praying towards Bayt Al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), Al-Bara' ibn Marur instructed that his face be turned towards the direction of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), towards the Kabah. He also bequeathed one-third of his wealth.
Thus, this practice became a Sunnah (established tradition)."
